stories.title: High intensity interval training modulates autophagy and apoptosis related markers in the liver of D galactose induced aged rats
stories.description: Aging deregulates autophagy and apoptosis, leading to progressive liver dysfunction. This study examined the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on autophagy and apoptosis-related markers in a D-galactose (D-gal)-induced aging model, focusing on the AMPK signaling pathway. Male Wistar rats were allocated into four experimental groups: Control (CTL), HIIT, D-gal, and D-gal+HIIT. Experimental aging was induced by D-galactose administration for eight weeks, while HIIT was performed using a treadmill running protocol. mRNA expression and protein levels of AMPK, Beclin1, NF-κB (p65), ATG9, and caspase-3 were assessed by real-time PCR and Western blotting, respectively. Total antioxidant and total oxidant status were determined using colorimetric methods. Pro-inflammatory indices were measured by ELISA. AMPK mRNA expression and p-AMPK protein levels were higher in the D-gal+HIIT group than in the D-gal group. HIIT upregulated Beclin1 and ATG9 expression at both the mRNA and protein levels and reduced caspase-3 mRNA expression and cleaved caspase-3 protein levels in the D-gal group. HIIT was associated with a reduction in NF-κB mRNA expression and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β levels, along with restoration of oxidant/antioxidant balance in D-gal-treated rats. These findings suggest that HIIT is associated with coordinated molecular changes that may help maintain liver homeostasis during experimental aging.
